requirements.title: Interoperable procedures may be defined by C-side means or by Fortran subprograms
requirements.source: S18.10.1 p1.definition-by-c-or-fortran; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF545.
requirements.definition: An interoperable procedure may be defined either by means other than Fortran or by means of a Fortran subprogram.

pending.interoperable-procedure-definition-by-co: Fortran-calls-C analogue after guarding C_INT > 0 before any C_INT-kind declaration: C defines int c_value_add_one(int x) with prototype int c_value_add_one(int), Fortran declares integer(c_int) function c_value_add_one(x) bind(C, name="c_value_add_one") with integer(c_int), value :: x, calls c_value_add_one(41), and expects 42. A companion reference-dummy analogue defines void c_set_ref(int *y), Fortran declares subroutine c_set_ref(y) bind(C, name="c_set_ref") with integer(c_int) :: y, initializes y to -11 before the call, and expects y == 7 after C stores *y = 7.
pending.interoperable-procedure-definition-by-fo: C-calls-Fortran analogue after guarding C_INT > 0 before any C_INT-kind declaration: Fortran defines integer(c_int) function f_value_add_one(x) bind(C, name="f_value_add_one") with integer(c_int), value :: x returning x+1, C declares int f_value_add_one(int), calls f_value_add_one(41), and observes 42. A companion reference-dummy analogue defines Fortran subroutine f_set_ref(y) bind(C, name="f_set_ref") with integer(c_int) :: y assigning y = 7; C declares void f_set_ref(int *y), initializes int y = -13, calls f_set_ref(&y), and observes y == 7.
